headlines.description: A video taken on Friday shows a driverless Waymo trying to navigate around a CHP traffic break on a Bay Area freeway. The footage has caused a lot of online buzz, rekindling the debate over how autonomous vehicles respond in emergency situations. The video has now reached millions online, and it’s triggering questions about Waymos and how they encounter the more complicated traffic situations on Bay Area freeways. “I think for a lot of individuals, it’s our nightmare to be stuck in the back of an autonomous driving car that is either breaking the law or driving you into danger and you have no recourse,” AJ said. AJ and her friend Holly were riding along northbound I-280 on Friday when the CHP initiated a traffic break to clear debris from the road. “Usually when you’re driving behind a blockade, you’re 1 or 2 miles back and you don’t get to see anything, but since we were in the first row, we decided to pull out a camera and film to see if we would see anything interesting,” AJ said. The video, which has gathered more than 3.3 million views, shows a Waymo attempting to get around the CHP patrol cars as the cruisers try to hold traffic back. Ultimately, an officer swerves to block the vehicle from passing. In a statement to NBC Bay Area, the CHP confirmed that multiple officers used their cruisers to block the Waymo’s path. The CHP also says the driverless Waymo ultimately complied and stayed back with traffic. This isn’t the first time Waymo has faced questions about how its vehicles respond to unexpected road conditions and hazards. During a major San Francisco power outage in 2025, there were multiple complaints about driverless cars freezing in intersections. After Fourth of July fireworks this year, officials raised concerns about Waymo vehicles blocking San Francisco streets as crowds left the area. Waymo has not yet responded to our requests for comment on this latest video but has previously said it works with first responders to continuously improve how its vehicles respond to various traffic hazards and situations. The company also noted it has remote assistance and emergency response teams that can respond rapidly. As for AJ, who shot the latest video, the video represents a bump in the road, not a reason to reopen the debate over the driverless vehicles. “I think it’s a work in progress, so they are going to have to make adjustments,” AJ said. CHP said it has had no communication with Waymo about this incident. It is unknown whether there was a passenger inside the Waymo at the time. Technology Jul 30 San Francisco Jul 16 San Francisco Jul 6 San Francisco transit overwhelmed: July 4 crowds cause hours-long BART, Caltrain and Waymo delays
